item.title: Dylan Harper expects to start season with hot hand
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper works on his jumper at practice at Madison Square Garden in New York, Wednesday, June 10, 2026, ahead of Game 4 of the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'll enter the nationally televised opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday night "very confident" in his outside shot after hitting a team-high 57.1% from 3-point range on 3.5 attempts in the preseason. The Spurs host the Blazers in a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference finals, won by the Spurs in seven games, at 8:30 p.m. at the Frost Bank Center. "I've worked at it all summer, so there's no reason for me to be hesitant," Harper said of his perimeter shooting. "No reason to pull back. Biggest thing is just taking the right shots at the right time." The 20-year-old second-year pro drafted No. 2 overall in 2025 led the Spurs in preseason scoring with a 14.8 average after tallying 19 points against the Sacramento Kings on 7 of 12 from the field (3 of 6 from distance) in a 126-97 victory on Friday in the preseason finale. Last season, he hit 34.3% from downtown on 2.6 attempts on his way to averaging 11.8 points. "Through the year last year, (his outside shot) was incrementally improving, and he's a ridiculously talented young player who has really matured and really started to build a foundation of habits," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. With the Spurs starting a speedy, downhill three-guard lineup of Harper, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle to go along with Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama, the team needs Harper to shoot well from deep to help spread the floor. "I think shooting from the perimeter was a big thing for me" to work on in the offseason, Harper said. "And I think just getting more comfortable with my shot, get more comfortable shooting off the dribble, and just try to be as efficient as I can." item.title: Nahida Akter replaces Nigar Sultana as Bangladesh's new T20I captain, Sobhana Mostary named deputy
item.description: Nahida Akter has been appointed Bangladesh's new T20I captain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) confirming the decision to Cricbuzz on Sunday. Nahida succeeds Nigar Sultana, who stepped down from the role following the Asian Games to focus on her game. Sobhana Mostary has been named vice-captain of the side. Nahida Akter Takes Over T20I Leadership “We sat with members of the selection panel along with others and decided to hand over the T20I captaincy to Nahida. Sobhana Mostary will be her deputy,” Rafiqul told Cricbuzz on Sunday. The board believes Nahida's experience in the leadership group makes her the right choice to lead the T20I team. The left-arm spinner had served as Bangladesh's vice-captain since Sultana was appointed captain in 2022. “Nahida has been the vice-captain for a pretty long time and now we feel the time is right to give her the responsibility of our T20I squad,” Rafiqul added. Nigar Sultana to Continue as Bangladesh's ODI Captain Sultana's decision to relinquish the T20I captaincy will not affect her role in the 50-over format. The wicketkeeper-batter will continue to lead Bangladesh in ODIs, having captained the team during their recent three-match tour of Australia. The BCB was reportedly caught off guard by Sultana's decision. It is understood that the former T20I captain was disappointed with the way she had been treated by the board in recent times, prompting her to step away from the leadership role in the shortest format. Bangladesh's Next Assignment Bangladesh's next assignment will be the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy in Thailand, where their campaign is scheduled to begin against Pakistan on November 12. The tournament will provide Nahida with an early opportunity to establish herself as captain and guide the team in her new role.

item.title: Patriots vs. Jets live updates: Score, news, discussion for NFL Week 6
item.description: Coming off their most dominant win of the season, the New England Patriots (3-2) are now looking to extend their win streak to three. Standing between them and that goal is a familiar opponent: the New York Jets (2-3), who themselves are entering Week 6 off a victory. From that perspective, the setup seems perfect for a highly-contested game. That said, the Patriots are clear favorites at home: not only have they looked like one of the best teams in the NFL the last two weeks, they also have gotten some significant reinforcements lately. Wide receiver A.J. Brown is back off injured reserve, while cornerback Christian Gonzalez is making his comeback from a two-game absence. Add the fact that left tackle Will Campbell and running back TreVeyon Henderson have both been cleared for the contest as well, and you can see why the home team earning a third straight W is the projected outcome. Will the Patriots indeed be able to do so, however? Let’s find out together. Welcome to our Patriots-Jets live tracker and community discussion. Live score: Patriots 0 : 3 Jets Sunday, Oct. 18, 1 p.m. ET | Gillette Stadium (Foxborough, MA) | Broadcast information | Game day roster | Inactives | Weather forecast First Quarter Winning the coin toss, the Patriots started the game on defense — and slowly. The unit gave up first-down pass plays to tight ends Mason Taylor and wide receiver Garrett Wilson before some runs by Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis brought the Jets into the New England red zone. The drive eventually stalled, but the visitors still took a 3-0 lead on a 42-yard field goal. | Patriots 0 : 3 Jets A.J. Brown was part of the Patriots’ offensive starting lineup, and the target of Drake Maye’s first pass attempt. However, the throw was batted at the line of scrimmage to end the team’s first possession in a three-and-out fashion. Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Florida State (Prev 10): Florida State may be the best 3-4 team in decades. They outplayed Miami for much of the game, but Malachi Toney came up with too many big plays down the stretch to push the game into overtime. The star receiver THREW for a 2-point conversion in the second OT to give Miami an 8-point lead. An unfortunate, non-obvious holding penalty erased an FSU TD that would have given them a chance to force triple OT with a two-point conversion of their own. QB Ashton Daniels was excellent. He threw for 3 TDs and ran for another while accumulating 329 total yards. He was a low-cost transfer portal add that everyone including me scoffed at. He has been really impressive. They get an open date before hosting Clemson. We’ll see if they’re heartbroken and quit after the rivalry loss or if they’ve proven they can compete with the best and rally from here. Norvell’s hot seat watch will be fascinating. 7. Virginia Tech (Prev 9): Ethan Grunkemeyer has been a very solid starting QB for the Hokies. No, the Hokies aren’t ready to compete for the 12-team playoff ( maybe not if the upcoming 24-teamer was starting in 2026 — which you can hear about here ), but this has been an impressive, rapid turnaround under Coach Franklin. They go to Clemson next week in a game that will draw storylines and serve as a de facto ACC Championship elimination game. The NFL has confirmed that the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers will play their Week 7 matchup in Paris as scheduled, despite escalating protests across France. The league’s decision comes amid growing security concerns ahead of its first regular-season game in the country. The historic matchup is scheduled for Sunday, October 25, at Stade de France, with kickoff at 9:30 a.m. ET. According to Front Office Sports, the NFL issued a statement Sunday addressing preparations and security arrangements. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters,” the league said. The NFL added that both teams are receiving regular updates and that league sites have experienced no disruptions. The statement followed another weekend of widespread demonstrations across France. Approximately 550,000 people participated in Saturday’s protest, according to the BBC. Authorities also made at least 1,200 arrests amid escalating violence. Demonstrators have raised concerns about rising living costs and proposed education spending cuts. Videos from Paris showed police deploying tear gas and water cannons as confrontations intensified. Despite those developments, the NFL has not announced any changes to the game or its surrounding events. The matchup represents another milestone in the league’s international expansion, with Paris joining its growing list of regular-season destinations. It will also mark the sixth of nine international games scheduled for the 2026 season. For the Saints and Steelers, preparations remain unchanged as both organizations await further security updates. The NFL’s position remains clear: Sunday’s game is proceeding as planned, although officials continue monitoring conditions in France. item.title: Why Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Texans debut was bigger than the stats
item.description: It will be some time before the Houston Texans and their fans can assess whether the team's recent trade for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be worth the hefty price. But no one is going to grumble about MHJ's debut. The Texans defeated their AFC South rivals, the division-leading Jacksonville Jaguars , 34-31 on Sunday, Oct. 18, when Ka'imi Fairbairn drilled a game-winning, 49-yard field goal as time expired to avert overtime. Harrison didn't have a major statistical impact on the game, catching three passes for 34 yards. But, with just a few practices under his belt, he was a significant component of a Houston pass game that carried the offense against a stout Jags defense. “Marvin Harrison Jr. – they brought him in, he had no really time to practice, and he did exactly what they needed him to do,” said former former Pro Bowl defensive tackle Gerald McCoy, now an NFL Network analyst, said on “GameDay Final.” Harrison's three catches matched his season high with the Arizona Cardinals, and his 34 yards represented his second-best output of the season in that department. “He had three first-down catches today," McCoy said. "He’s a big-bodied receiver, and they needed him to go in, catch the ball, help us move the chains, and they did that today. I’m excited to see what this team has moving forward, because that defense will be better. If the offense is rolling like this, everybody look out for the Texans.” All the NFL news on and off the field. Sign up for USA TODAY's 4th and Monday newsletter . item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 17: Andrew Rappleyea #87 of the Penn State Nittany Lions runs for yardage against Zeke Berry #10 of the Michigan Wolverines during the first half of a college football game at Michigan Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images So, I guess that was fun for a half, no? Not really? Oh well, let’s just go ahead and get this over with… Quarterback: F Rocco Becht almost single-handedly lost Penn State the game with his three turnovers, all of which led to Michigan cashing in for touchdowns. That’s your difference-maker, right there. Running Back: C- Carson Hansen had a TD run in what was otherwise another unremarkable game on the ground from the running backs, as PSU rushed for a total of 65 yards on 30 carries for a whopping 2.2 rushing yards. Wide Receiver: B+ Chase Sowell has been the lone Iowa State transfer who has actually turned out to be worth the hype at this point. Sowell had a whopping 11 catches for 151 yards and a TD, and probably would’ve had more if he had a better QB throwing him the ball. Brett Eskildsen also caught three balls for 29 yards. Tight End: C+ The tight ends in total, caught 12 balls for 78 yards as PSU, with Andrew Rappleyea leading the way with seven catches and 34 yards, as part of Taylor Mouser opting for a quicker, shorter, passing attack. Offensive Line: C Not the worst, but not the greatest performance ever for this group. Let’s just cut the difference and call it a C. Defensive Line: D Once again, there was a lack of pressure generated from the front lines, not to mention how badly they got pushed around once Bryce Underwood got benched. Linebacker: C Poor Tony Rojas, he could have been balling out at Miami right now helping the Hurricanes get back to the national championship game and win it all this time around. Instead, he’s stuck with putting together performances like his team-leading 12 total tackles, including two for a loss and a sack in yet another losing effort. Secondary: A- Michigan was held to just 90 yards passing, as Zion Tracy had an interception off a wild ricochet and Josiah Zayas had an Odell Beckham Jr.-like pick right before halftime to snuff out what likely would’ve been a scoring drive for Michigan. Speaking of Zayas, the true freshman has been one of the few bright spots on this team and deserves the biggest bag possible to keep him around in Happy Valley. Special Teams: B+ Ryan Barker nailed his lone field goal attempt and Nathan Tiyce had a couple of nice punts to pin Michigan deep in their own red zone. Coaching: F Hey, did you know if your starting quarterback is struggling, looking incompetent, and absolutely holding your team back, you can bench him for somebody else? Kyle Whittingham got that memo, but apparently Matt Campbell didn’t.

item.title: Manchester United miss chance to make statement after turbulent week with draw at Leeds
item.description: A 1-1 draw at Elland Road in January 2026 for a Manchester United side with a back three and framed by some incendiary comments about Jason Wilcox precipitated the departure of a manager. A repeat result is less likely to bring the same outcome, not least because Michael Carrick was not the one criticising the director of football. Yet when it seemed Carrick might be turning a corner, that his side were set for their finest result of a stuttering season and that his players were, as he claimed, galvanised by the events of the last week , United lost another lead and the chance to deliver a statement on the pitch. Compared to the injury-time goals Everton and Tottenham scored, at least there was no late letdown for United – not with Noussair Mazraoui clearing off the line from Anton Stach in the 92nd minute – but they can summon different types of disappointment. Even as, after adopting Ruben Amorim ’s favourite system – probably not a tribute to the Portuguese, even if his valedictory game came against Leeds – they looked more solid in open play, they have now conceded three set-piece goals in Yorkshire already this season, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin ’s equaliser. It is a reason why their wait for a Premier League clean sheet goes on. And, indeed, why their wait for a win does. They have shared the points in their last three top-flight games but, in all competitions, they are without a victory in six matches. Even Amorim never went six without winning, if a triumph on penalties is factored in. “We are not getting too carried away, because we didn’t win, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons you get what you deserve in the end,” said Carrick. “It wasn't a perfect performance, it wasn't our most unbelievable performance, but there was definitely a lot in there that you can show how together the group were. It felt like a fresh start today.” But without the result which would have demonstrated that. So it did not get worse for Carrick, though there was insufficient evidence to argue it got much better. United had too little threat after conceding. They did not have that much before, either, but at least there was some solidity in a 3-4-3 system, with a back three shielded by twin defensive midfielders. A repeat result is less likely to bring the same outcome, not least because Michael Carrick was not the one criticising the director of football. Yet when it seemed Carrick might be turning a corner, that his side were set for their finest result of a stuttering season and that his players were, as he claimed, galvanised by the events of the last week , United lost another lead and the chance to deliver a statement on the pitch. Compared to the injury-time goals Everton and Tottenham scored, at least there was no late letdown for United – not with Noussair Mazraoui clearing off the line from Anton Stach in the 92nd minute – but they can summon different types of disappointment. Even as, after adopting Ruben Amorim ’s favourite system – probably not a tribute to the Portuguese, even if his valedictory game came against Leeds – they looked more solid in open play, they have now conceded three set-piece goals in Yorkshire already this season, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin ’s equaliser. It is a reason why their wait for a Premier League clean sheet goes on. And, indeed, why their wait for a win does. They have shared the points in their last three top-flight games but, in all competitions, they are without a victory in six matches. Even Amorim never went six without winning, if a triumph on penalties is factored in. “We are not getting too carried away, because we didn’t win, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons you get what you deserve in the end,” said Carrick. “It wasn't a perfect performance, it wasn't our most unbelievable performance, but there was definitely a lot in there that you can show how together the group were. It felt like a fresh start today.” But without the result which would have demonstrated that. So it did not get worse for Carrick, though there was insufficient evidence to argue it got much better. United had too little threat after conceding. They did not have that much before, either, but at least there was some solidity in a 3-4-3 system, with a back three shielded by twin defensive midfielders. Dominic Calvert-Lewin sealed a point for Leeds (Getty) A half-time lead lent itself to the suggestion their players should criticise Jason Wilcox more often. Two of the players bought by Wilcox combined for the goal. Perhaps, deep in the defence, Lisandro Martinez was celebrating the recruitment he had lamented. But the Argentinian’s eventful week came to an early, and anticlimactic, end as he went off at half-time; if nothing else, that may have spared him the post-match interviews. United were breached soon after Mazraoui replaced Martinez; even with three centre-backs, none were near Leeds’ likeliest scorer when he got his fourth goal in five games. Calvert-Lewin ran away from Carlos Baleba and held off Bryan Mbeumo when he met Nico Elvedi’s header and hooked in a shot. They had failed to heed the warning from an earlier set-piece from Stach, with Senne Lammens saving Elvedi’s first-half header. And there was a spirit and a resilience to Leeds, now only beaten in six of their last 32 league matches, and only by champions Arsenal this season. Yet they were below their best. “It says a lot that we are even slightly disappointed with a point against Manchester United,” manager Daniel Farke said. “You always have to be aware, it is still Manchester United. Many, many compliments to my players for a dominant performance against Man United.” The outspoken Lisandro Martinez was hooked at half-time (Reuters) He noted the team that switched shape because of the opposition was in fact United. “It says a lot about how much respect we've earned,” the German said. Carrick only called it a “tweak” but it at least offered indications he can change. His United have floundered against sides with a back three, so he borrowed from Amorim’s infamous fondness for the formation. At times, it seemed United had no centre-forward; at others, it was Mbeumo. Youri Tielemans , signed as a central midfielder, has looked better when others play that role. He was in the front three, and integral in the supply line. “I am really impressed with Youri,” Carrick said. United led when Mbeumo poked in a shot from Tielemans’ low centre. The same combination had almost brought an earlier breakthrough, with Tielemans’ quality apparent in the inside-right channel as the unmarked Mbeumo headed wide from the Belgian’s cross. “Bryan gives so much to the team,” said Carrick. With Benjamin Sesko injured, Marcus Rashford unused and Matheus Cunha limited to a cameo, Mbeumo had to. United’s new look was a more defensive one. It still did not lend itself to either a shutout or a victory.

item.title: Did Thunder’s Sam Presti tell Kevin Durant about James Harden trade? The mystery is solved
item.description: DOUG HOKE/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Did Thunder’s Sam Presti tell Kevin Durant about James Harden trade? Sam Presti never gave Kevin Durant a heads-up before trading James Harden to the Houston Rockets in 2012. That’s according to veteran NBA journalist Jonathan Abrams. It seems to have finally answered a question that has lingered over the Oklahoma City Thunder ’s franchise history for more than a decade. Speaking via The NBA Base, Abrams revealed that he directly asked Durant whether Presti had discussed the blockbuster move with him beforehand. Kevin Durant revealed Sam Presti did not consult him before trading James Harden to Houston in 2012, per @Jpdabrams "It’s interesting because I asked Kevin directly whether Presti discussed trading James with him before making the move. Kevin said, 'Sam has probably grown since… pic.twitter.com/GwMppR3nlg — NBABase (@TheNBABase) October 18, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Kevin said, ‘Sam has probably grown since then, but no, back then I just played basketball; he didn’t talk to me about those moves,'” Abrams recalled. The revelation offers a revealing glimpse into Oklahoma City’s front-office philosophy at the time. Fresh off a run to the 2012 NBA Finals, the Thunder appeared poised to contend for years with Durant, Russell Westbrook, and Harden leading the way. Troy Taormina-Imagn Images However, contract negotiations with Harden stalled over approximately $4.5 million. That prompted Presti to trade the reigning Sixth Man of the Year to Houston just before the regular season. The decision reshaped the franchise and helped launch Harden’s rise into an MVP-caliber superstar. Meanwhile, it left Oklahoma City to build around Durant and Westbrook. Presti has since established himself as one of basketball’s most influential executives. After beginning his career with the San Antonio Spurs, he took charge of the Seattle SuperSonics’ front office in 2007 and oversaw the transition to Oklahoma City. His drafting of Durant, Westbrook, and Harden helped propel the Thunder to the Finals. Years later, a new rebuild brought Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren, and Jalen Williams into the fold. That patient approach culminated in Oklahoma City’s 2025 championship .Kevin Durant has finally shed light on one of the Thunder’s most consequential decisions. item.title: Jamel Dean Gets Nod as Steelers Captain vs. Former Team
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Jamel Dean in a game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now TAMPA, Fla. — Ahead of Sunday’s road matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, cornerback Jamel Dean and running back Travis Homer served as the Pittsburgh Steelers’ captains at the coin toss. Dean played the first seven seasons of his NFL career with the Buccaneers before signing with Mike McCarthy’s team as a free agent in the offseason. Dean joked earlier this week about having to make sure not to go “on autopilot” and walk into the home locker room at Raymond James Stadium. The Steelers switched to a weekly captain format under McCarthy. “I think Mike believes in … everybody has leadership abilities,” Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said. “And I think there’s gotta be a way to foster that, and it’s great opportunities, for young guys, especially, or special teamers to lead. Because it doesn’t always have to be the best player on the team, or the oldest player on the team, or the guy with the most Pro Bowls, or the guy who’s been on the team the longest to lead. Young players need to step up and lead.” Homer, another offseason addition, made his mark as a special teamer with the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears. Alan Saunders provided reporting from Tampa. item.description: Carrick says draw with Leeds felt like a ‘fresh start’ for Man Utd Michael Carrick believes Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Leeds felt like a “fresh start” as he praised the attitude and response of his players. Carrick was particularly pleased with the impact of United’s midfield duo of Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, who he feels are adapting well to the demands of playing for the club. “They’re both young players adapting to life at this football club and I thought both of them were terrific today and I thought they both did really well in midweek,” Carrick said. “That’s a massive positive for us.” The United boss felt there was a different mentality around the group heading into the game and was encouraged by the way his players responded. “It felt like a bit of a fresh start, if I’m honest, today, with where we’re at, accepting it and doing something about it,” he said. “It definitely shows that the boys are desperate to do well for each other as much as anything else and how much they appreciate playing for this football club. “There was a real purpose to the group over the last couple of days and they took it onto the pitch. “That’s a tough game today and it can find you out pretty quickly but the boys stood up to it really well.” Carrick admitted United are still some way from where they want to be, but remains convinced they can turn their form around. “We’re not accepting that anything is great by any stretch so I’m realistic with that,” he said. “But sometimes you do struggle and you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet and we’ve got to find a way through it. “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time where it can go in different directions and we’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.” He added: “I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it a certain way but I’ve got no doubts that we can go on a good run. “If we keep doing the right things I still think we can have a really good season.”

item.title: Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals Gunner Stockton’s defiant reaction to blowing Auburn game
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals Gunner Stockton’s defiant reaction to blowing Auburn game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Georgia football looked like the clear top-ranked team in college football after taking down Alabama on the road a week ago, but life comes at you fast in this sport. On Saturday, Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs were on the wrong end of a shocking upset, as unranked Auburn took down Georgia 27-24 between the hedges in Athens. Auburn, despite the flaws that it has shown throughout the season, played an excellent game on Saturday in all facets. However, turnovers proved to be the deciding factor that pushed the Tigers over the top . Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw a pair of interceptions and gave away a back-breaking fumble in the fourth quarter that allowed Auburn to kick the game-winning field goal. After the game, Smart talked about his quarterback and his reaction to costing his team the game against one of its bitter rivals, via Mark Schlabach of ESPN. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I saw him in the locker room,” Smart said. “His head was up. I mean, we wouldn’t have been in the position we were in if it wasn’t for Gunner. I’m really proud that he’s growing up and getting better. He had all the success last week, and so many people want to reach out and talk about it. It’s tough.” Stockton is usually very solid for Georgia and has been exactly that since he became the starter, so it was a bit surprising to see him be so careless with the football on Saturday. Auburn’s defense has not played very well at any point this season, so that made Georgia’s offensive struggles even more of the surprise. Despite this surprising loss, Georgia will still be very highly ranked and still has all of its goals in front of it this season. There are no unbeaten teams left in the SEC, so a conference title is still on the table for Smart and company. Georgia has a bye week in Week 8. Smart and company will be back in action in Week 9 in a rivalry game against Florida where Stockton will be trying to get back on track. item.title: When Juventus expects Yildiz to be back in latest update
item.description: When Juventus expects Yildiz to be back in latest update Juventus are still waiting for Kenan Yildiz to return to action after his surgery at the start of the season , with the attacker remaining one of the club’s most important players. His absence has been felt, and the Bianconeri are eager to have him back as they look to remain competitive across all competitions. The club are doing their best to maintain its level while Yildiz continues his recovery. Juventus want to ensure the team remains in a strong position so that his return can provide a boost rather than come with the pressure of rescuing their campaign. Juventus continue to miss Yildiz Yildiz has established himself as a key figure at Juventus and appears comfortable with the expectations that come with his role. His performances have demonstrated his importance to the team, making his absence particularly difficult as the club navigates the season without him. The Bianconeri are counting down to his return, but it appears supporters will need to remain patient. His recovery is expected to take longer than just a few days or weeks, leaving Juventus to manage his absence while he works towards full fitness. According to Tuttojuve , Juventus expect Yildiz to remain sidelined until the start of December. That timeline means his return could still be some way off, depending on how his recovery progresses over the coming weeks. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) The Bianconeri will not rush his recovery There is also a possibility that Yildiz could miss the remainder of the calendar year if his recovery does not go according to plan. Such an outcome would be a significant setback for Juventus, given the influence he has had on the team. However, the club are understood to be unwilling to rush him back before he is ready. While they would welcome his return as soon as possible, ensuring that he recovers properly remains the priority. Juventus believe the final month of the year could be an appropriate target for his comeback. That would give Yildiz more time to complete his rehabilitation and return when he is ready to contribute again. Until then, the Bianconeri must find ways to cope without one of their most important players . His return would provide a welcome boost, but Juventus appear prepared to remain patient rather than risk bringing him back too soon.

item.title: Something unusual stopped the Jaguars-Texans game in London
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars-Houston Texans game in London came to an unexpected stop Sunday morning, and it had nothing to do with an injured player. Umpire Larry Smith went down during the first quarter at Wembley Stadium and eventually had to be carted from the field. NBC Sports reported that Smith slipped on the wet grass between plays. Smith fell backward while trying to retrieve the football. He briefly got up but went down again after trying to walk. Trainers from both teams came onto the field before Smith was placed on a cart. He tipped his cap to the Wembley crowd as he left, according to The Sporting News . The NFL was able to keep the game going with six officials instead of the usual seven. NBC Sports reported the league has a system for such situations, with other members of the crew taking over some of the missing umpire’s responsibilities. Smith is in his second NFL season after previously officiating college football and the USFL. Before the injury, Jacksonville and Houston were scoreless. Houston later struck first when quarterback C.J. Stroud connected with tight end Foster Moreau for a 6-yard touchdown . The extra point gave the Texans a 7-0 advantage. Houston won the game 34-31. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season. Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
